questions.stem: What is the result of the expression `true || false && false`?
questions.explanation: The AND operator has higher precedence than OR, so `false && false` is evaluated first, resulting in false. However, due to short-circuit evaluation, `true || false` results in true because OR only needs one true operand.

questions.stem: Explain how short-circuit evaluation affects the execution of logical expressions in programming.
markingGuide: Explains that it prevents unnecessary evaluation of the second operand.
Provides an example where short-circuit evaluation changes the program behavior.
questions.explanation: Short-circuit evaluation means that in a logical expression, the second operand is not evaluated if the first operand is sufficient to determine the result. For instance, in `false && (x > 0)`, the condition `(x > 0)` is not evaluated because the result is already false. This can prevent errors or improve performance by avoiding unnecessary calculations.

questions.stem: Describe the difference between operator precedence and associativity, providing examples for each.
markingGuide: Defines operator precedence and provides an example.
Defines associativity and provides an example.
Explains how both affect the evaluation order in expressions.
questions.explanation: Operator precedence determines the order in which different operators are evaluated in an expression. For example, in `3 + 4 * 2`, multiplication has higher precedence than addition, so it is evaluated first. Associativity, on the other hand, determines the order of evaluation for operators of the same precedence. For instance, in `10 - 5 - 2`, subtraction is left-associative, so it is evaluated as `(10 - 5) - 2`.
